name: Hawaii

statute.readVia: https://web.archive.org/web/20251224191826/https://www.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2025/bills/HB226_CD1_.HTM (archived copy of the official bill text, which rewrites the whole section) + governor message GM1229 (Act 129, signed 2025-05-29); capitol.hawaii.gov answers 403 to scripts

windshield.strip: film not encroaching on the AS-1 portion; if no AS-1 marking, no lower than 4 inches below the top of the windshield
windshield.reflective: mirrored or highly reflective finishes showing red, yellow, amber or blue from outside are banned

frontSide.note: plus or minus 6%, measured with the glazing

backSide.note: exempt on sedans, vans, minivans, trucks or buses if rearview mirrors on both sides (Act 129, 2025 extended this to sedans)

rear.note: exempt on sedans, vans, minivans, trucks, buses or other motor vehicles if rearview mirrors on both sides

tint.measuredHow: film + glass combined ('when used in conjunction with the glazing material')

reflectivity.front: no mirrored or highly reflective finish showing red, yellow, amber or blue

tint.dualMirrors: Rear and rear side window exemption applies only if the vehicle has rearview mirrors on both sides.
tint.certificateOrSticker: Installer must issue a certificate of compliance, which the owner keeps in the vehicle; a missing certificate is prima facie evidence of installer noncompliance (§ 291-21.5(f)).

medicalExemption.text: No medical exemption found in § 291-21.5 as read via mirror.

penalty.text: Owner: $300 to $550 per offense; installer: $700 to $1,200 per offense plus free reinstallation or reimbursement. Occupants must fully roll down tinted windows when stopped by police (noncriminal infraction otherwise).

tint.lastAmended: 2025 (Act 129, H.B. 226 C.D. 1, signed 2025-05-29, effective on approval)
quotes: have a light transmittance of no less than thirty-five per cent plus or minus six per cent
no lower than four inches below the top of the windshield ... if no AS-1 markings can be found in the left or right upper margin of the windshield
Rear windows, including the rear windshield on sedans, vans, minivans, trucks, buses, or other motor vehicles
side windows to the rear of the driver on sedans, vans, minivans, trucks, or buses ... provided that the vehicles are equipped with rearview mirrors on both sides
No less than $300 and no more than $550 for each separate offense if the person is the owner of the motor vehicle that is in violation

helmet.conditions: Operators and passengers under 18 on motorcycles or motor scooters

handheldPhone.noviceOrAgeBan: Drivers under 18 may not use a mobile electronic device even hands-free (except to call 911)

radarDetector.note: commercial vehicles over 10,001 lb banned federally (49 CFR 392.71)

openQuestions: capitol.hawaii.gov answers 403 to scripts; § 291-21.5 read on the archived copy of the official H.B. 226 C.D. 1 text (2025-12-24) and governor message GM1229 (Act 129); § 286-81 and § 291C-137 on archived copies of the official HRS pages (2025-02-13, 2025-08-22).
Medical exemption: none found in § 291-21.5; Hawaii may handle it elsewhere - not confirmed.
§ 291C-137 fine amount not read directly (a search excerpt of the official text mentions $300, higher in school/construction zones) - left null.
Studded tires, underglow, lift-height: not found.
